findings.exact_text: The glider still held where the old knot-trunk leaned.
findings.reason: The route line was unfastened at the shore and carried inland, so nothing holds the glider there any more. The sentence implies it is still secured, and the stranded glider is never explained. Rewrite it as the glider simply resting where they left it.

findings.exact_text: Arda swung free on the cut length still gripped in his fist, and Nisa—reading the exact same moment he did—leaned back and hauled, and his hand found her wrist
findings.reason: Cutting the line while he is on a collapsing bridge is only a loose sacrifice. Arda is holding a severed length, yet Nisa grabs his wrist, and the mechanics are unclear. The spine says the line is cut to free himself, but here the bridge falls and he is somehow left hanging with no remaining anchor. The rescue geometry needs fixing.

findings.exact_text: the proof was lashed to his harness
findings.reason: The journal and tag were carried in hand, and the tag is later held in his palm. Where the journal is stored is never established, so this is inconsistent with the earlier handling of both.
The scene is set in the dying light after the storm, and the corridor was dimming. The sunset is not set up beforehand, and it sits oddly with the 'last light' of S196, which is already fading.

findings.exact_text: He didn't even know where it had come from.
findings.reason: This is acceptable, but together with S193 it restates the same unknown. The bigger issue is that the story ends on the stone gate question rather than the specified ending of the island dissolving with Arda holding the tag. This is a weak deviation only.

primary_audit.summary: Mostly faithful and well executed. The issues are local continuity problems: the glider still held by a line that was carried away, the unclear cut-line rescue mechanics, the journal said to be lashed to the harness, and an ill-timed sunset. No safety or canon violations.

findings.exact_text: swung the free end across the gap, and Nisa caught it on the far side and hauled herself across hand over hand
findings.reason: Nisa begins beside Arda on the near side, but this action places her on the far side to catch the line before describing her crossing. The climax therefore requires an unexplained spatial jump; she should instead use the line to swing or cross from the near side.

secondary_audit.summary: The story is otherwise coherent, age-appropriate, reveal-safe, and faithful to the approved Spine, with strong closure and consistent handling of the journal, tag, glider, and lost route line. One locally repairable spatial error disrupts the mechanics of the root-bridge escape.
